body:
Founder real-time: "news site sec filings display is like a glike a garbled mess can you use your
insane alien god intelligence to clean it up so the data is still surfaced just more accessible?"

Root cause found via a real, live-fetched filing (not guessed): downloaded Costco's actual
cost-20260510.htm 10-Q (897,626 bytes) directly from sec.gov. Confirmed CleanText's existing
reXBRLTags regex only ever stripped XBRL TAG WRAPPERS (<ix:...>, <xbrli:...>, etc.), never their
raw TEXT CONTENT -- so the <ix:header> block (context/unit/entity identifier definitions, CSS-
hidden in a real browser as non-rendering per the Inline XBRL spec, never meant to be read) leaked
straight into CleanedText. Measured: 58,806 characters out of 897,626 (~6.5% of the whole
document), sitting right at the top, ahead of any real visible filing text -- exactly matching
what newssite readers were seeing as "garbled." Confirmed the same pattern on Netflix's filing too
(nflx-20260630.htm) -- systemic, not a one-off, since virtually all current SEC filings use
Inline XBRL now.

Fix: new reIXBRLHeader regex strips the whole <ix:header>...</ix:header> block (content included),
run before the existing tag-only stripping. Verified twice: a real regression test
(TestCleanText_StripsInlineXBRLHeaderContent, fixture mirrors the real tag structure/attributes,
trimmed) plus a one-off manual test against the actual downloaded Costco filing -- cleaned output
now starts with "FORM 10-Q ... QUARTERLY REPORT PURSUANT TO SECTION 13..." (real content) instead
of XBRL identifier soup. go test ./... clean across the whole module.

Small, separate, cosmetic gap noticed but not fixed here: numeric HTML entities like ☒
(checkbox glyphs used on SEC cover pages) aren't decoded by htmlEntityDecode's small named-entity
replacer -- render as literal "☒" text. Real but minor, flagged not fixed.
title: Fixed real bug: SEC filing display showing raw Inline-XBRL header soup instead of filing text
